locator: The Unreality of Time, conclusion: 'Whenever we judge anything to exist in time, we are in error'
interpretation: McTaggart concludes that the A series is contradictory, that time involves change and change the A series, so that nothing really changes; yet we do judge and perceive things as in time, and so perceive them as they are not. Read as: nothing is being moved, and there are judgings and perceivings. The final paragraph raises the retorsion itself ('must it not be to an appearance which changes ... and is not time, then, shown to be real after all?') and promises an answer; that answer (The Nature of Existence II) is not pinned. 'Change' is McTaggart's A-series change, which is narrower than or different from reduction from potency to act (DISAMB-MOTION).
